parsed.explanation: The unit responds to a vertical border where a smooth, uniform surface on the left meets a fine, high-contrast dotted or granular texture on the right, such as knit, polka dots, speaker grilles, keypads, QR codes, or thatch.
parsed.evidence: Almost all 20 crops show a plain region on the left and a dot or speckle texture filling the right half, across unrelated objects and colours. parsed.missing_data: Synthetic tests with a dot texture placed left versus right of a plain region, and texture alone versus edge alone, would confirm that both the boundary and the side matter.

CP_s3.explanation: Responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine, repeated dot-like texture on the right, such as polka dots, knit stitches, perforations, studs or speckles.

parsed.explanation: Responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine, repeated dot-like texture on the right, such as polka dots, knit stitches, perforations, studs or speckles.
parsed.evidence: Nearly all 20 crops show a plain area on the left and a dense dotted or bumpy texture on the right (#1 knit, #2 and #13 perforations, #6 and #19 polka dots, #10 keypad, #16 leopard print). parsed.missing_data: Activations on synthetic stimuli that vary which side the texture is on and the texture type (dots vs. stripes) would test the left/right edge-plus-texture account; it would also help to know why random photos still reach 4-7.
